title: An Efficient FPGA-Based Hardware Accelerator of Fully Quantized Mamba-2
problem: Mamba-2 inference exhibits element-wise operations that underutilize GPU tensor cores, reducing efficiency. Research on full-quantization strategies for Mamba-2 is lacking.
motivation: Mamba-2 is a promising state space model architecture offering improved accuracy and training speed, but efficient hardware acceleration is essential for practical deployment.
method: The team built Hfqmamba2 using a reconfigurable FPGA (a chip you can reprogram for specific tasks) instead of a GPU. They employ hybrid-precision quantization, reducing some numbers to fewer bits more aggressively than others to save space and computation. To avoid expensive calculations, they included a segmented lookup table that approximates RMSNorm's inverse square root operation—a normalization step—without computing it fully each time. The design pipelines SSM operations (Mamba-2's state-machine calculations) so different layers run in parallel, all validated on an Alveo U50 FPGA board.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining a reconfigurable FPGA with lookup-table approximations and selective-precision quantization to efficiently run Mamba-2 where GPUs with tensor cores struggle on element-wise operations.
contributions: Hybrid-precision full-quantization strategy (Hfqmamba2) for Mamba-2 with acceptable accuracy loss
Reconfigurable FPGA architecture using segmented quantization and lookup tables for RMSNorm operations
Intra-layer computation pipeline design for selective SSM layer processing
Two hardware configurations achieving 114.05× CPU speedup and 29.81× GPU speedup

metrics.speedup: 114.05× vs CPU, 29.81× vs PyTorch GPU, 1.94× vs official CUDA
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 282.75× vs CPU, 297.87× vs PyTorch GPU, 35.89× vs official CUDA
